A string's pitch can be calculated.
Dans son Harmonie universelle, Mersenne: In his Harmonie universelle, Mersenne links a string's pitch to its length, its tension and its thickness.
Guido d'Arezzo nomme les notes: Guido of Arezzo names the notes
Ut, ré, mi, fa, sol, la : les notes ont: Ut, re, mi, fa, sol, la: the notes get names.
Dans une lettre au moine Michel de Pompo: In a letter to the monk Michael of Pomposa, Guido is credited with the idea of taking the syllables from the hymn Ut queant laxis, each line of which starts one note higher.
Philolaos et les rapports des sons: Philolaus and the ratios of sounds
Le pythagoricien Philolaos décrit l'octa: The Pythagorean Philolaus describes the octave (2/1) divided into a fifth (3/2) and a fourth (4/3). The accounts that credit Pythagoras himself with the discovery are unreliable.
Glaréan ajoute l'ionien et l'éolien: Glarean adds the Ionian and the Aeolian
Les futurs majeur et mineur entrent dans: The future major and minor enter music theory.
Dans son Dodecachordon, le Suisse Heinri: In his Dodecachordon, the Swiss Heinrich Glarean takes the modes from eight to twelve. The Ionian matches our major scale, the Aeolian the natural minor.
Tout son périodique est une somme de sin: Every periodic sound is a sum of sine waves.
Joseph Fourier publie sa Théorie analyti: Joseph Fourier publishes his Analytical Theory of Heat. The tool, designed for heat, is now used to analyze every recorded sound.
Rameau publie son Traité de l'harmonie: Rameau publishes his Treatise on Harmony
An inverted chord is still the same chord.
Rameau y décrit les renversements et la: Rameau describes inversions and the fundamental bass, which become the grammar of classical harmony.
Douze demi-tons égaux, calculés au chiff: Twelve equal semitones, calculated to the digit.
Le prince chinois Zhu Zaiyu calcule au b: The Chinese prince Zhu Zaiyu computes the twelfth root of 2 on an abacus to 24 exact decimals: twelve perfectly equal semitones.
L'oreille n'entend pas toutes les fréque: The ear does not hear all frequencies alike.
Avec des écouteurs, Harvey Fletcher et W: Using headphones, Harvey Fletcher and Wilden Munson measure how much intensity each frequency needs to seem equally loud.
